# **Delta checkpoint file format**

A delta checkpoint is a **two-file canonical HuggingFace checkpoint directory**: one or more model-NNNNN-of-NNNNN.safetensors shards plus a model.safetensors.index.json. Each version directory represents one sync's worth of *changed* tensors, encoded as byte-level XOR deltas against the previous version and zstd-compressed. The directory is **self-describing** — the shard uses no custom format; only the index carries the delta metadata.

## **Directory layout**

A checkpoint contains multiple files. The most important files are the following:

```
weight_v000001/
├── model-00000-of-00001.safetensors  # shards: compressed XOR deltas, opaque U8
└── model.safetensors.index.json      # version metadata + tensor→file map
```

**File numbering:** model-{offset:05d}-of-{total:05d}.safetensors, sequential across PP-source ranks with no gaps. A single-shard checkpoint (one PP-src rank with changes) is 00000-of-00001.

Besides these files, the publisher may publish additional metadata like tensor\_map through other files.

Sample files: [https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1K5Bh5Dw\_wpTBWAOvZclyvK6imVfNp35q?usp=drive\_link](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1K5Bh5Dw_wpTBWAOvZclyvK6imVfNp35q?usp=drive_link) 

## **Shard file: model-NNNNN-of-NNNNN.safetensors**

Standard safetensors binary layout — no format extension is used:

**Safetensors shard byte layout**

![][image1]

Copied from [https://huggingface.co/docs/safetensors/en/index\#format](https://huggingface.co/docs/safetensors/en/index#format) 

The header is ordinary JSON, with two kinds of entries.

### **\_\_metadata\_\_ — per-tensor checksums**

A flat dict\[str, str\] mapping each *changed* tensor name to its **adler32 hexdigest** (8 hex chars), computed over the tensor's **new full weight** — not the delta, not the compressed bytes:

```json
"__metadata__": {
  "model.language_model.embed_tokens.weight": "a9ace35e",
  "model.language_model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight": "8281b1c4"
}
```

The checksum is the apply-time integrity check: the engine recomputes adler32 of the resulting weight after applying the delta and **raises on mismatch**.

### **Tensor entries — opaque U8 blobs**

One per changed tensor, carrying only the three standard fields. The true dtype/shape are **not** preserved here:

```json
"model.language_model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight": {
  "dtype": "U8",
  "shape": [1704248],
  "data_offsets": [0, 1704248]
}
```

* **dtype** is always U8 — the stored bytes are opaque to safetensors.  
* **shape** is always 1-D, \[N\] where N is the *stored* byte count.  
* **data\_offsets** are byte offsets into the data region. Offsets across tensors are contiguous with no gaps; their sum equals the data-region size exactly.

### **Stored bytes — a standalone zstd frame per tensor**

Each tensor's byte span is a **standalone zstd frame**. Every blob begins with the zstd magic 28 b5 2f fd (LE 0x28B52FFD) and decompresses independently. Compression is **zstd level 1** (not a knob). Decompressing a blob yields the XOR delta new ^ old over the tensor's flat byte view:

stored bytes  \=  zstd\_compress\_level1( new.view(uint8) ^ old.view(uint8) )

The encoding is **byte-level and dtype-blind**: weights are reinterpreted as uint8 and XORed elementwise. The same path works for any dtype (BF16, FP8, quantized) without per-dtype logic. The true dtype and shape live elsewhere — the engine recovers them from its local checkpoint's own tensor metadata, since the apply is in-place onto an existing weight of known shape.

**Sparsity** of the decompressed delta varies by tensor: the embedding (large, barely changed) is \~0.1% nonzero; dense layers 3–22%. Aggregate density lands in slime's typical 1–3% range, which is what makes the format worth it.

## **Index file: model.safetensors.index.json**

```json
{
  "metadata": {
    "version": "000001",
    "base_version": "000000",
    "delta_encoding": "xor",
    "compression_format": "zstd",
    "checksum_format": "adler32"
  },
  "weight_map": {
    "model.language_model.embed_tokens.weight": "model-00000-of-00001.safetensors",
    "model.language_model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight": "model-00000-of-00001.safetensors"
  }
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- |
| version | This checkpoint's version, 6-digit zero-padded. |
| base\_version | The version this delta applies onto. A version refuses to apply unless the local checkpoint is at this base — out-of-order or double application is rejected. |
| delta\_encoding | xor (default) or overwrite. xor stores new ^ old (involution — apply exactly once). overwrite stores changed positions \+ absolute new values (idempotent — re-applying converges). |
| compression\_format | Always "zstd" (hardcoded; not a knob). |
| checksum\_format | adler32 (this file), xxh3-128 (default), or blake3. Selects the algorithm behind the \_\_metadata\_\_ checksums. |
| weight\_map | tensor\_name → shard file. Only changed tensors are listed. |

weight\_map lists only tensors that changed this sync; tensors absent from the map are unchanged and not stored. **A version with no delta metadata in its index is an ordinary full HF checkpoint** — pulling it as-is resets the chain, so a late-joining host seeds from the newest full version instead of replaying deltas.

**About the check sum:** 

The trainer writes, per tensor, adler32 (**new\_bytes**) — the checksum of the result, not of the delta blob. A checksum of the delta blob would only prove the delta survived transport. A checksum of the new bytes proves the entire reconstruction equation held end-to-end: **old ⊕ delta \== what the trainer had in memory**. One cheap check therefore catches, indistinguishably but fail-closed:

* a corrupted or truncated delta blob (zstd usually catches this first, but not always),  
* a wrong base — stale working copy, syncs applied out of order, a partially-applied previous sync, a drifted byte anywhere in the 2 TB base,  
* any bug in the reconstruction code itself (the rust XOR, offset math, dtype handling).

The key point here is that in order to validate the check sum of each tensor in delta version N+1,  actual tensors of version N are needed at delta application time. 

Adler32 is not the only check sum algo.  Slime recently added more options and they recently changed the default algo to xxh3-128.

## **Apply semantics (engine side)**

To reconstruct version N on a host holding base version N−1:

1. **Read.** For each tensor in weight\_map: seek to data\_offsets, read the span, zstd-decompress → XOR delta bytes.  
2. **Apply.** Read the corresponding tensor from the local base checkpoint, reinterpret both as uint8, XOR in place: new \= delta ^ old. The XOR is an involution — it must be applied **exactly once** against the correct base; applying twice reverts.  
3. **Verify.** Recompute adler32 of the resulting new bytes and compare to \_\_metadata\_\_\[name\]. Mismatch → raise (corrupt delta or wrong base).  
4. **Reload.** Once all tensors verify, reload the patched local checkpoint through the ordinary update\_weights\_from\_disk path — the engine's weight loader is unaware of the delta format.

Because the encoding is byte-level and the dtype/shape come from the existing local weight, the format is **lossless and bit-identical** for any dtype, including quantized checkpoints, with no arithmetic and no floating-point drift.

## **Variant: overwrite encoding** 

This is not a priority for now

When delta\_encoding is overwrite instead of xor, each stored blob (before zstd) is a packed \[u32 count, u32 positions..., values...\]:

\[nnz : u32\] \[pos\_0, pos\_1, ..., pos\_{nnz-1} : u32 each\] \[new values at those positions, original dtype\]

The engine scatters the new values into the named positions. Larger on the wire and a less cache-friendly scattered apply, but **idempotent** — re-applying or finishing a partial apply converges to the same state regardless of count. Use it when re-applicability matters more than wire size. Checksum and compression are identical to the xor path.

## **References**

This format is **not** a Hugging Face format. It is a slime (THUDM) convention layered on plain safetensors; the authoritative definition is slime's source and docs, not HF user documentation.

* **Format spec (writer)** — [slime/backends/megatron\_utils/update\_weight/update\_weight\_from\_disk\_delta.py](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/blob/main/slime/backends/megatron_utils/update_weight/update_weight_from_disk_delta.py):  \_write\_delta\_files (index \+ shard layout) and \_encode\_delta (diff/XOR/zstd).  
* **Checksum & encoding helpers** — [slime/utils/disk\_delta.py](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/blob/main/slime/utils/disk_delta.py):  \_Adler32, overwrite\_encode, checksum.  
* **Slime user doc reference** — [Delta Weight Sync docs](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/blob/main/docs/en/advanced/delta-weight-sync.md): the closest thing to a format reference; written as feature docs.  
* **Engine-side reader (apply)** — SGLang PR \#26519: [github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26519](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26519) — \_apply\_delta, \_maybe\_zstd\_decompress (zstd magic 0x28B52FFD auto-detect).  
* **Independent context** — Changyi Yang, "Delta Weight Sync" (June 2026): [changyi.fun/posts/delta-weight-sync](https://changyi.fun/posts/delta-weight-sync/) — third-party walkthrough of the converging delta-sync work, including slime.
